title: Following Tubby to Chicago in 1918 and the stockyard job
summary: Tubby and others went to the Deluxe Cafe in Chicago; Hall and his parents were sent for, he walked off a stockyard job and took his brother's place when Tubby was drafted.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, they went up there, and they had a band at the Deluxe Cafe. Lawrence Dewey with them. That's right, I think Lawrence Dewey had a band at that time, yeah. So he was up there working with them at the Deluxe Cafe at 35th and State, a fellow by the name of Shaw. And so about later on my oldest brother went up to Chicago, but he wasn't a musician. So that left my mother, my father, and myself still in New Orleans. So that's when he sent for the three of us. When I first went up to Chicago, I didn't have any job playing, but in the meantime my oldest brother was working at Stockyard, and he had charge of the laundry department or something there. So when I went up there, he told me to come out one morning to see about a job, which I did, and the job that they give me was in the spare room department, and all the floor was full of water. He had to walk in the water, and I didn't even have no boots. So I walked out the next fire escape and went home. So I didn't do anything. In the meantime, my brother got drafted in World War I. That's when I got my chance. I'd taken his place.
And you both went to Chicago the same trip, the same time?
No, no. The turbine went ahead of me.
Oh, when you said the three of you went, I didn't know.
No, my father and mother and myself. I see. They sent to the three of you.
Yes, I see. Your older brother sent to the three of you.
Is your older brother already there?

Yeah, he went up with Tebberway. But he was a musician. So after I got around, I got introduced to some of the fellas around, and I played a few little jobs, and I can't think who it is now. But anyhow, when my brother got drafted, and him and my oldest brother went at the same time, and so that's why I'd taken his place.
You were too young to get them involved.
